Dividing the weighted moments by their respective weights and expanding to first order in t/Ut/U gives

Ep\displaystyle E_{p} =U/4+εNN​(𝐤)/21/2−δ𝐤=U2+(1+d)​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/U),\displaystyle=\frac{U/4+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})/2}{1/2-\delta_{\mathbf{k}}}=\frac{U}{2}+(1+d)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/U), (S53)
Eh\displaystyle E_{h} =−U/4+εNN(𝐤)/21/2+δ𝐤=−U2+(1+d)​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/U).\displaystyle=\frac{-U/4+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})/2}{1/2+\delta_{\mathbf{k}}}=-\frac{U}{2}+(1+d)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/U).

The atomic contributions ±U/2\pm U/2 therefore cancel in (Ep+Eh)/2(E_{p}+E_{h})/2, while the same residue imbalance shifts both normalized sector centers by U​δ𝐤=d​εNN​(𝐤)U\delta_{\mathbf{k}}=d\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k}). This yields

𝒞𝐤=(1/2+2​CNN)​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/U).\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf{k}}=(1/2+2C_{\mathrm{NN}})\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/U). (S54)

From Eq. S54 to the GZ.

The GZ contains both the average moment center and the weight-imbalance term. Substituting Eqs. S47 and S54 into Eq. S18 shows their cancellation explicitly:

ωGZ(U)​(𝐤)=[(1/2+2​CNN)+(2​CNN−1/2)]​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/U)=4​CNN​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/U).\boxed{\begin{aligned} \omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}^{(U)}(\mathbf{k})&=\left[(1/2+2C_{\mathrm{NN}})+(2C_{\mathrm{NN}}-1/2)\right]\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/U)\\ &=4C_{\mathrm{NN}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/U).\end{aligned}} (S55)

The spin-independent +εNN(𝐤)/2+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})/2 contribution to the moment center is cancelled by the −εNN(𝐤)/2-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})/2 contribution from δ𝐤​Δ𝐤\delta_{\mathbf{k}}\Delta_{\mathbf{k}}. In contrast, the two spin-correlation terms, each 2​CNN​εNN​(𝐤)2C_{\mathrm{NN}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k}), add. The factor near 1.4 is therefore not a renormalized hopping chosen from the GZ curve; it is fixed by two complementary first-moment contributions governed by the same bond spin correlation.

At the resolution used for the Green functions, the periodic spin background has energy E0≃−11.229E_{0}\simeq-11.229 for 16 sites, giving

CNN≃−0.351,sNN=4​CNN≃−1.404.C_{\mathrm{NN}}\simeq-0.351,\qquad s_{\mathrm{NN}}=4C_{\mathrm{NN}}\simeq-1.404. (S56)

This value comes from a single periodic 4×44\times 4 Heisenberg exact diagonalization, not from averaging over the continuous mixed-momentum sectors. At order t2/Ut^{2}/U, every such sector produces the same exchange Ji​j=4​|ti​j|2/UJ_{ij}=4|t_{ij}|^{2}/U: the sector-dependent hopping phases cancel between the forward and reverse virtual hops. An average would therefore return the identical correlator in the U→∞U\to\infty limit. Table S2 verifies the approach of the directly extracted root to this first-moment result.

For the thermodynamic square-lattice spin-1/21/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet, the high-precision ground-state energy is e0≃−0.669e_{0}\simeq-0.669 for J=1J=1 [33]. Because there are two nearest-neighbor bonds per site,

CNN∞=e0/2≃−0.335,sNN∞=4​CNN∞=2​e0≃−1.339.C_{\mathrm{NN}}^{\infty}=e_{0}/2\simeq-0.335,\qquad s_{\mathrm{NN}}^{\infty}=4C_{\mathrm{NN}}^{\infty}=2e_{0}\simeq-1.339. (S57)

This thermodynamic spin-background value is distinct from the finite momentum-mixing-resolution correlator that determines the calculated asymptote. We expect the latter to approach the thermodynamic value as the momentum-mixing resolution is increased.

5.1 Extension to arbitrary hopping classes

The preceding calculation does not rely on the bond being nearest neighbor. Resolve the kinetic energy into symmetry-equivalent hopping classes bb,

Ht=∑bHtb,εb(𝐤)=−tb∑𝜹∈bei​𝐤⋅𝜹,Cb=⟨𝐒i⋅𝐒i+𝜹⟩𝜹∈b.H_{t}=\sum_{b}H_{t_{b}},\qquad\varepsilon_{b}(\mathbf{k})=-t_{b}\sum_{\bm{\delta}\in b}e^{i\mathbf{k}\cdot\bm{\delta}},\qquad C_{b}=\langle\mathbf{S}_{i}\cdot\mathbf{S}_{i+\bm{\delta}}\rangle_{\bm{\delta}\in b}. (S58)

Applying the Schrieffer–Wolff and Hellmann–Feynman steps above to one bond in class bb gives

gb≡⟨ci​σ†​ci+𝜹,σ⟩=2​tbU​(14−Cb)+O⁡(tmax2/U2).g_{b}\equiv\langle c^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}c_{i+\bm{\delta},\sigma}\rangle=\frac{2t_{b}}{U}\left(\frac{1}{4}-C_{b}\right)+O(t_{\max}^{2}/U^{2}). (S59)

The coordination of class bb enters through the displacement sum in εb\varepsilon_{b}; it is not an additional prefactor. Fourier transformation of Eq. S59 therefore gives the particle–hole weight imbalance

δ𝐤=n𝐤​σ−12=1U​∑b(2​Cb−12)​εb​(𝐤)+O⁡(tmax2/U2).\delta_{\mathbf{k}}=n_{\mathbf{k}\sigma}-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{U}\sum_{b}\left(2C_{b}-\frac{1}{2}\right)\varepsilon_{b}(\mathbf{k})+O(t_{\max}^{2}/U^{2}). (S60)

To obtain the moment center without assuming that particle–hole symmetry divides the dispersive first moment equally, write

Mp=U4+mp,Mh=−U4+mh,mp+mh=∑bεb​(𝐤),M_{p}=\frac{U}{4}+m_{p},\qquad M_{h}=-\frac{U}{4}+m_{h},\qquad m_{p}+m_{h}=\sum_{b}\varepsilon_{b}(\mathbf{k}), (S61)

where a momentum-independent midgap shift has been removed. Using wp=1/2−δ𝐤w_{p}=1/2-\delta_{\mathbf{k}} and wh=1/2+δ𝐤w_{h}=1/2+\delta_{\mathbf{k}}, expansion of the normalized moments gives

Ep\displaystyle E_{p} =U/4+mp1/2−δ𝐤=U2+2​mp+U​δ𝐤+O⁡(tmax2/U),\displaystyle=\frac{U/4+m_{p}}{1/2-\delta_{\mathbf{k}}}=\frac{U}{2}+2m_{p}+U\delta_{\mathbf{k}}+O(t_{\max}^{2}/U),
Eh\displaystyle E_{h} =−U/4+mh1/2+δ𝐤=−U2+2​mh+U​δ𝐤+O⁡(tmax2/U).\displaystyle=\frac{-U/4+m_{h}}{1/2+\delta_{\mathbf{k}}}=-\frac{U}{2}+2m_{h}+U\delta_{\mathbf{k}}+O(t_{\max}^{2}/U). (S62)

Consequently,

𝒞𝐤=Ep+Eh2=∑bεb​(𝐤)+U​δ𝐤+O⁡(tmax2/U),Δ𝐤=U+O⁡(tmax).\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf{k}}=\frac{E_{p}+E_{h}}{2}=\sum_{b}\varepsilon_{b}(\mathbf{k})+U\delta_{\mathbf{k}}+O(t_{\max}^{2}/U),\qquad\Delta_{\mathbf{k}}=U+O(t_{\max}). (S63)

Substitution of Eqs. S60 and S63 into the shared GZ identity, Eq. S18, exposes the cancellation for each hopping class:

ωGZ​(𝐤)\displaystyle\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}(\mathbf{k}) =∑bεb​(𝐤)+2​U​δ𝐤+O⁡(tmax2/U)\displaystyle=\sum_{b}\varepsilon_{b}(\mathbf{k})+2U\delta_{\mathbf{k}}+O(t_{\max}^{2}/U)
=∑b[1+2​(2​Cb−12)]​εb​(𝐤)+O⁡(tmax2/U)\displaystyle=\sum_{b}\left[1+2\left(2C_{b}-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]\varepsilon_{b}(\mathbf{k})+O(t_{\max}^{2}/U)
=4​∑bCb​εb​(𝐤)+O⁡(tmax2/U).\displaystyle=4\sum_{b}C_{b}\varepsilon_{b}(\mathbf{k})+O(t_{\max}^{2}/U). (S64)

Thus, at leading order,

ωGZ​(𝐤)=4​∑bCb​εb​(𝐤).\boxed{\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}(\mathbf{k})=4\sum_{b}C_{b}\varepsilon_{b}(\mathbf{k})}. (S65)

The two terms proportional to 2​Cb2C_{b} add, while the spin-independent +εb/2+\varepsilon_{b}/2 and −εb/2-\varepsilon_{b}/2 pieces cancel. This is the origin of the common factor 44. It is unrelated to coordination: a third-neighbor hopping class contributes 4​C3​N​ε3​N4C_{\mathrm{3N}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{3N}}, even when its displacement set contains a different number of bonds.

6 CDW-side derivation and hopping-channel charge rule

For U=0U=0 and V≫tV\gg t, the half-filled atomic background alternates doubly occupied and empty sites. Move one electron from a doubly occupied source to a neighboring empty target. In the intermediate configuration, interactions with the three other occupied neighbors of the target cost 3​(2​V)3(2V), and the source–target bond contributes VV. The virtual hopping denominator is therefore

Δhop=3​(2​V)+V=7​V.\Delta_{\mathrm{hop}}=3(2V)+V=7V. (S66)

To make explicit why no additional many-body correlator multiplies this denominator, choose one of the two atomic checkerboard product states |C⟩|C\rangle and orient a nearest-neighbor bond from a doubly occupied site i∈Ai\in A to an empty site j∈Bj\in B. For a fixed spin, define the normalized one-hop defect |bi​j,σ⟩=cj​σ†​ci​σ​|C⟩|b_{ij,\sigma}\rangle=c^{\dagger}_{j\sigma}c_{i\sigma}|C\rangle. To apply first-order perturbation theory explicitly, split H=H0+HtH=H_{0}+H_{t}, where H0H_{0} contains the atomic density interaction and Ht=−t∑⟨l​m⟩​τ(cl​τ†cm​τ+H.c.)H_{t}=-t\sum_{\langle lm\rangle\tau}(c^{\dagger}_{l\tau}c_{m\tau}+\mathrm{H.c.}). The defect is an eigenstate of H0H_{0} with Eb−EC=7​VE_{b}-E_{C}=7V. The term −t​cj​σ†​ci​σ-tc^{\dagger}_{j\sigma}c_{i\sigma} in HtH_{t} gives ⟨bi​j,σ|Ht|C⟩=−t\langle b_{ij,\sigma}|H_{t}|C\rangle=-t, so its Rayleigh–Schrödinger coefficient is

⟨bi​j,σ|Ht|C⟩EC−Eb=−t−7​V=t7​V.\frac{\langle b_{ij,\sigma}|H_{t}|C\rangle}{E_{C}-E_{b}}=\frac{-t}{-7V}=\frac{t}{7V}.

The distinct one-hop Fock states are orthogonal. Moreover, HtH_{t} has no matrix element between the two atomic checkerboard states at first order, so choosing either state is sufficient for this local calculation. The standard first-order wave function and its bond coherence are therefore

⟨bi​j,σ|bi​j,σ⟩\displaystyle\langle b_{ij,\sigma}|b_{ij,\sigma}\rangle =⟨C|ni​σ​(1−nj​σ)|C⟩=1,\displaystyle=\langle C|n_{i\sigma}(1-n_{j\sigma})|C\rangle=1,
|ΨC⟩\displaystyle|\Psi_{C}\rangle =|C⟩+∑b⟨b|Ht|C⟩EC−Eb​|b⟩+O⁡(t2/V2)\displaystyle=|C\rangle+\sum_{b}\frac{\langle b|H_{t}|C\rangle}{E_{C}-E_{b}}|b\rangle+O(t^{2}/V^{2})
=|C⟩+t7​V​∑⟨i∈A,j∈B⟩σ|bi​j,σ⟩+O⁡(t2/V2),\displaystyle=|C\rangle+\frac{t}{7V}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\langle i\in A,j\in B\rangle\\ \sigma\end{subarray}}|b_{ij,\sigma}\rangle+O(t^{2}/V^{2}),
⟨ΨC|ci​σ†​cj​σ|ΨC⟩\displaystyle\langle\Psi_{C}|c^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}c_{j\sigma}|\Psi_{C}\rangle =t7​V​[⟨C|ci​σ†​cj​σ|bi​j,σ⟩+⟨bi​j,σ|ci​σ†​cj​σ|C⟩]+O⁡(t3/V3)\displaystyle=\frac{t}{7V}\left[\langle C|c^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}c_{j\sigma}|b_{ij,\sigma}\rangle+\langle b_{ij,\sigma}|c^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}c_{j\sigma}|C\rangle\right]+O(t^{3}/V^{3})
=t7​V​⟨C|ci​σ†​cj​σ​cj​σ†​ci​σ|C⟩+O⁡(t3/V3)\displaystyle=\frac{t}{7V}\langle C|c^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}c_{j\sigma}c^{\dagger}_{j\sigma}c_{i\sigma}|C\rangle+O(t^{3}/V^{3})
=t7​V​⟨C|​ni​σ​(1−nj​σ)​|C⟩+O⁡(t3/V3)=t7​V+O⁡(t3/V3).\displaystyle=\frac{t}{7V}\langle C|n_{i\sigma}(1-n_{j\sigma})|C\rangle+O(t^{3}/V^{3})=\frac{t}{7V}+O(t^{3}/V^{3}). (S67)

The second cross term in the square brackets vanishes because cj​σ​|C⟩=0c_{j\sigma}|C\rangle=0, whereas the first reverses precisely the hop that created |bi​j,σ⟩|b_{ij,\sigma}\rangle. The norm of |ΨC⟩|\Psi_{C}\rangle differs from unity only at O⁡(t2/V2)O(t^{2}/V^{2}), so normalization changes this O⁡(t/V)O(t/V) coherence first at O⁡(t3/V3)O(t^{3}/V^{3}). The factor multiplying t/(7​V)t/(7V) is therefore exactly one: in the atomic checkerboard state ni​σ=1n_{i\sigma}=1 and nj​σ=0n_{j\sigma}=0 for either spin. Both an empty site and an on-site doublon carry zero spin, so there is no degenerate bond-spin background whose overlap must be averaged. This is the essential difference from the Mott state, where two singly occupied sites have a fluctuating singlet–triplet composition and the allowed virtual-hop weight is the singlet projector, producing 1/4−⟨𝐒i⋅𝐒j⟩1/4-\langle\mathbf{S}_{i}\!\cdot\!\mathbf{S}_{j}\rangle. Here the doublon–empty bond fixes the spin matrix element kinematically; the two spin channels give the same unit factor (their spin-summed coherence is 2​t/(7​V)2t/(7V)). Spin correlations induced in the virtual defect have weight O⁡(t2/V2)O(t^{2}/V^{2}) and do not modify the leading O⁡(t/V)O(t/V) coherence. Moreover, the bipartite gauge transformation that reverses the sign of tt also reverses this bond coherence, so only odd powers occur and the next correction is O⁡(t3/V3)O(t^{3}/V^{3}). The translated checkerboard product state gives the same local matrix element, as does the translation-symmetric combination of the two used in the calculation.

The momentum dependence follows directly by Fourier transforming this bond coherence. The on-site contribution remains ⟨ni​σ⟩=1/2\langle n_{i\sigma}\rangle=1/2, while the four directed NN displacements give

n𝐤​σ\displaystyle n_{\mathbf{k}\sigma} =12+2​gNN​(cos⁡kx+cos⁡ky)+O⁡(t3/V3)\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}+2g_{\mathrm{NN}}(\cos k_{x}+\cos k_{y})+O(t^{3}/V^{3}) (S68)
=12−17​V​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t3/V3),\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{7V}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{3}/V^{3}),

where gNN=t/(7​V)+O⁡(t3/V3)g_{\mathrm{NN}}=t/(7V)+O(t^{3}/V^{3}) from Eq. S67 and εNN​(𝐤)=−2​t​(cos⁡kx+cos⁡ky)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})=-2t(\cos k_{x}+\cos k_{y}). The zeroth-moment identity therefore gives

δ𝐤=n𝐤​σ−12=−17​V​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t3/V3).\delta_{\mathbf{k}}=n_{\mathbf{k}\sigma}-\frac{1}{2}=-\frac{1}{7V}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{3}/V^{3}). (S69)

It remains to identify which term of Eq. S18 survives at O⁡(t)O(t). At particle–hole symmetry, μ=4​V\mu=4V, the atomic addition and removal centers are +4​V+4V and −4​V-4V, so their separation retains the atomic value Δ𝐤=8​V+O⁡(t)\Delta_{\mathbf{k}}=8V+O(t). Particle–hole symmetry by itself maps addition at 𝐤\mathbf{k} to removal at 𝐐−𝐤\mathbf{Q}-\mathbf{k} and therefore does not fix the common center at the same momentum. We instead use the exact extended-Hubbard first-moment identity derived in Sec. 4.1. At U=0U=0 it reads ℳ1=Mp+Mh=εNN​(𝐤)−V​ℱ𝐤\mathcal{M}_{1}=M_{p}+M_{h}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})-V\mathcal{F}_{\mathbf{k}}, while ℳ1=𝒞𝐤−δ𝐤​Δ𝐤\mathcal{M}_{1}=\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf{k}}-\delta_{\mathbf{k}}\Delta_{\mathbf{k}} algebraically. To the order retained here, ℱ𝐤=δ𝐤=−εNN(𝐤)/(7V)\mathcal{F}_{\mathbf{k}}=\delta_{\mathbf{k}}=-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})/(7V). Hence

𝒞𝐤\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf{k}} =ℳ1+δ𝐤​Δ𝐤=εNN​(𝐤)−V​δ𝐤+8​V​δ𝐤+O⁡(t2/V)\displaystyle=\mathcal{M}_{1}+\delta_{\mathbf{k}}\Delta_{\mathbf{k}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})-V\delta_{\mathbf{k}}+8V\delta_{\mathbf{k}}+O(t^{2}/V) (S70)
=εNN(𝐤)+7Vδ𝐤+O(t2/V)=O(t2/V),Δ𝐤=8V+O(t).\displaystyle=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+7V\delta_{\mathbf{k}}+O(t^{2}/V)=O(t^{2}/V),\qquad\Delta_{\mathbf{k}}=8V+O(t).

The two O⁡(t)O(t) terms cancel exactly in the complete-sector first moment. Thus the leading GZ comes entirely from δ𝐤​Δ𝐤\delta_{\mathbf{k}}\Delta_{\mathbf{k}}; unlike the Mott case, there is no second O⁡(t)O(t) contribution from 𝒞𝐤\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf{k}}. This statement is specific to NN hopping at t′=0t^{\prime}=0: a same-sublattice NNN hop can propagate the pre-existing charge defect and therefore enters 𝒞𝐤\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf{k}} at first order, as derived below. Substitution into Eq. S18 gives

ωGZ(V)​(𝐤)=−17​V​εNN​(𝐤)​(8​V)+O⁡(t2/V)=−87​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/V).\boxed{\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}^{(V)}(\mathbf{k})=-\frac{1}{7V}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})(8V)+O(t^{2}/V)=-\frac{8}{7}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/V).} (S71)

The calculated VV-axis sequence converges monotonically to this parameter-free value.

The local argument generalizes to a bipartite lattice of coordination zz. The virtual defect costs (2​z−1)​V(2z-1)V, whereas the addition–removal separation is 2​z​V2zV, yielding

ωGZ(V)​(𝐤)=−2​z2​z−1​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/V).\boxed{\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}^{(V)}(\mathbf{k})=-\frac{2z}{2z-1}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/V).} (S72)

Unlike the Mott-side coefficient, the leading CDW-side number depends only on local coordination and does not require a nontrivial thermodynamic correlation estimate.

6.1 Charge rule for separate hopping channels and numerical check

For nonzero next-nearest-neighbor hopping, write the bare dispersion as

εNN(𝐤)=−2t(coskx+cosky),εNNN(𝐤)=−4t′coskxcosky.\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})=-2t(\cos k_{x}+\cos k_{y}),\qquad\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NNN}}(\mathbf{k})=-4t^{\prime}\cos k_{x}\cos k_{y}. (S73)

The two hopping contributions act differently in the atomic checkerboard background. The NN operator connects opposite sublattices and creates the 7​V7V defect counted in Eq. S66; combining its weight imbalance with the 8​V8V addition–removal separation gives the coefficient −8/7-8/7.

A NNN hop instead connects sites on the same checkerboard sublattice. Let |𝐑,+⟩|\mathbf{R},+\rangle denote a particle-addition defect on the empty sublattice and |𝐑,−⟩|\mathbf{R},-\rangle a particle-removal defect on the occupied sublattice, and let P±P_{\pm} project onto the corresponding one-defect manifolds. To first order in t′t^{\prime}, projection of the hopping operator gives

P+​Ht′​P+\displaystyle P_{+}H_{t^{\prime}}P_{+} =∑𝐤εNNN(𝐤)|𝐤,+⟩⟨𝐤,+|,\displaystyle=\sum_{\mathbf{k}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NNN}}(\mathbf{k})|\mathbf{k},+\rangle\langle\mathbf{k},+|, (S74)
−P−​Ht′​P−\displaystyle-P_{-}H_{t^{\prime}}P_{-} =∑𝐤εNNN(𝐤)|𝐤,−⟩⟨𝐤,−|.\displaystyle=\sum_{\mathbf{k}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NNN}}(\mathbf{k})|\mathbf{k},-\rangle\langle\mathbf{k},-|.

The minus sign in the second line is the signed particle-removal convention Eh<0E_{h}<0. Thus particle addition and removal acquire the same εNNN\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NNN}} contribution to their signed moment centers. The NNN term propagates a defect already present in the Lehmann sector, so it carries neither the 7​V7V virtual denominator nor a spin-overlap factor. It enters the common moment center, while the leading NN weight imbalance is unchanged. Consequently,

ωGZ(V)​(𝐤)=−87​εNN​(𝐤)+εNNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(tmax2/V).\boxed{\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}^{(V)}(\mathbf{k})=-\frac{8}{7}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NNN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t_{\max}^{2}/V).} (S75)

Frequencies are measured from the chemical potential. At nonzero t′t^{\prime}, where particle–hole symmetry no longer fixes the midpoint, a momentum-independent midgap shift is removed before the two hopping-channel coefficients are extracted; any remaining offset belongs to the indicated subleading correction.

Table S3 compares the coefficients obtained from the 120 unique path momenta with the independent strong-coupling predictions. The large residual of a single scale multiplying the complete bare tt–t′t^{\prime} band is visible directly in the curves; resolving the NN and NNN contributions removes that shape mismatch.

Each spectral group contains 121 plotted Γ\Gamma–XX–MM–Γ\Gamma rows, with the final Γ\Gamma repeating the first; coefficient extraction uses the 120 unique momenta. At each momentum we enumerate all sign changes of Re​G\mathrm{Re}\,G inside the central gap and track the continuous branch with low spectral weight. The six interaction-axis groups in Table S3 have a root at every unique momentum. In the finite-(U,V)(U,V) scans below, unavailable rows are omitted from coefficient extraction and are never interpolated into a fit.

7 Finite-interaction spectral reorganization and full scans

At fixed U=40U=40, the denser progression V/t=0,4,8,12,16,V/t=0,4,8,12,16, and 20 follows the growth of the Mott-side GZ dispersion and its transfer to the CDW-side branch while the central gap remains open. The left column gives ωGZ​(𝐤)\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}(\mathbf{k}) and the right column subtracts the corresponding V=0V=0 curve. The change is not a uniform shift: the dispersion grows on the Mott side and changes branch on the CDW side.

8 Finite-(U,V)(U,V) strong-coupling laws and numerical validation

8.1 Finite-(U,V)(U,V) Mott branch

In the atomic Mott background every site is singly occupied. A NN hop creates a doublon–holon pair. The on-site energy increases by UU, while the interaction energy of the hopped bond decreases from VV to zero; changes on the other six bonds cancel pairwise. The neutral virtual-defect energy cost is therefore

Δ​EM=U−V.\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}}=U-V. (S76)

The corresponding leading spin Hamiltonian is

Hspin=4​t2U−V​∑⟨i​j⟩(𝐒i⋅𝐒j−14)+O⁡(t3/(Δ​EM)2).H_{\rm spin}=\frac{4t^{2}}{U-V}\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\left(\mathbf{S}_{i}\cdot\mathbf{S}_{j}-\frac{1}{4}\right)+O\!\left(t^{3}/(\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}})^{2}\right). (S77)

Hellmann–Feynman differentiation with respect to one bond hopping gives

gM≡⟨ci​σ†​cj​σ⟩=2​tU−V​(14−CNN)+O⁡(t2/(Δ​EM)2).g_{\rm M}\equiv\langle c^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}c_{j\sigma}\rangle=\frac{2t}{U-V}\left(\frac{1}{4}-C_{\mathrm{NN}}\right)+O\!\left(t^{2}/(\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}})^{2}\right). (S78)

Writing d=2​CNN−1/2d=2C_{\mathrm{NN}}-1/2 and Fourier transforming yields

ℱ𝐤=δ𝐤=dU−V​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/(Δ​EM)2).\mathcal{F}_{\mathbf{k}}=\delta_{\mathbf{k}}=\frac{d}{U-V}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O\!\left(t^{2}/(\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}})^{2}\right). (S79)

Although the virtual hopping cost is Δ​EM=U−V\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}}=U-V, the atomic addition and removal poles remain at +U/2+U/2 and −U/2-U/2. The 4​V4V change in the local bond energy is cancelled by the 4​V4V part of μ=U/2+4​V\mu=U/2+4V, so

ΔM(0)=U.\Delta_{\rm M}^{(0)}=U. (S80)

Using Eqs. S27, S79, and S80, the normalized-sector center is

𝒞𝐤M\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf{k}}^{\rm M} =ℳ1+δ𝐤​ΔM(0)\displaystyle=\mathcal{M}_{1}+\delta_{\mathbf{k}}\Delta_{\rm M}^{(0)}
=εNN​(𝐤)+(U−V)​δ𝐤+O⁡(t2/Δ​EM)\displaystyle=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+(U-V)\delta_{\mathbf{k}}+O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}})
=(12+2​CNN)​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/Δ​EM).\displaystyle=\left(\frac{1}{2}+2C_{\mathrm{NN}}\right)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}}). (S81)

The GZ is consequently

ωGZM​(𝐤)\displaystyle\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}^{\rm M}(\mathbf{k}) =ℳ1+2​δ𝐤​ΔM(0)+O⁡(t2/Δ​EM)\displaystyle=\mathcal{M}_{1}+2\delta_{\mathbf{k}}\Delta_{\rm M}^{(0)}+O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}})
=[1+2​U−VU−V​(2​CNN−12)]​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/Δ​EM),\displaystyle=\left[1+\frac{2U-V}{U-V}\left(2C_{\mathrm{NN}}-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}}), (S82)

so that, in the form used in Eq. (8) of the main text,

sNNM​(U,V)=1+2​U−VU−V​(2​CNN−12)+O⁡(tΔ​EM).\boxed{s_{\mathrm{NN}}^{\rm M}(U,V)=1+\frac{2U-V}{U-V}\left(2C_{\mathrm{NN}}-\frac{1}{2}\right)+O\!\left(\frac{t}{\Delta E_{\mathrm{M}}}\right).} (S83)

8.2 Finite-(U,V)(U,V) CDW branch and moment-center cancellation

In the atomic checkerboard background, a NN hop takes one electron from a doubly occupied site to an empty site. The initial on-site energy UU is removed. In the intermediate state the target interacts with its three other doubly occupied neighbors at cost 3​(2​V)3(2V), and the source–target bond costs another VV. The neutral virtual-defect energy cost is therefore

Δ​EC=7​V−U.\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}}=7V-U. (S84)

First-order perturbation theory gives the directed per-spin coherence

gC=t7​V−U+O⁡(t2/(Δ​EC)2),g_{\rm C}=\frac{t}{7V-U}+O\!\left(t^{2}/(\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}})^{2}\right), (S85)

and hence

ℱ𝐤=δ𝐤=−17​V−U​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/(Δ​EC)2).\mathcal{F}_{\mathbf{k}}=\delta_{\mathbf{k}}=-\frac{1}{7V-U}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O\!\left(t^{2}/(\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}})^{2}\right). (S86)

At μ=U/2+4​V\mu=U/2+4V, adding one electron to an empty checkerboard site costs 8​V−μ=4​V−U/28V-\mu=4V-U/2. Removing one electron from a doublon costs μ−U=4​V−U/2\mu-U=4V-U/2. The signed atomic sector separation is therefore

ΔC(0)=8​V−U.\Delta_{\rm C}^{(0)}=8V-U. (S87)

The exact first-moment sum rule now gives

ℳ1​(𝐤)=εNN​(𝐤)−V​ℱ𝐤=εNN​(𝐤)−V​δ𝐤+O⁡(t2/Δ​EC)=8​V−U7​V−U​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/Δ​EC).\mathcal{M}_{1}(\mathbf{k})=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})-V\mathcal{F}_{\mathbf{k}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})-V\delta_{\mathbf{k}}+O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}})=\frac{8V-U}{7V-U}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}}). (S88)

It follows without assuming anything about the individual addition and removal dispersions at the same momentum that

𝒞𝐤C\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\mathbf{k}}^{\rm C} =ℳ1+δ𝐤​ΔC(0)\displaystyle=\mathcal{M}_{1}+\delta_{\mathbf{k}}\Delta_{\rm C}^{(0)}
=[8​V−U7​V−U−8​V−U7​V−U]​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/Δ​EC)\displaystyle=\left[\frac{8V-U}{7V-U}-\frac{8V-U}{7V-U}\right]\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}})
=O⁡(t2/Δ​EC).\displaystyle=O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}}). (S89)

This is the required O⁡(t)O(t) moment-center cancellation for the complete particle-addition and particle-removal sectors. Finally,

ωGZC​(𝐤)\displaystyle\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}^{\rm C}(\mathbf{k}) =ℳ1+2​δ𝐤​ΔC(0)+O⁡(t2/Δ​EC)\displaystyle=\mathcal{M}_{1}+2\delta_{\mathbf{k}}\Delta_{\rm C}^{(0)}+O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}})
=−8​V−U7​V−U​εNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(t2/Δ​EC),\displaystyle=-\frac{8V-U}{7V-U}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t^{2}/\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}}), (S90)

and therefore

sNNC​(U,V)=−8​V−U7​V−U+O⁡(tΔ​EC).\boxed{s_{\mathrm{NN}}^{\rm C}(U,V)=-\frac{8V-U}{7V-U}+O\!\left(\frac{t}{\Delta E_{\mathrm{C}}}\right).} (S91)

For U=0U=0, its leading term reduces to −8/7-8/7. Denoting the leading rational term by sNN,0Cs_{\mathrm{NN},0}^{\rm C} and writing x=U/(4​V)x=U/(4V),

sNN,0C=−8−4​x7−4​x=−87−449​x−16343​x2+O⁡(x3),s_{\mathrm{NN},0}^{\rm C}=-\frac{8-4x}{7-4x}=-\frac{8}{7}-\frac{4}{49}x-\frac{16}{343}x^{2}+O(x^{3}), (S92)

so the first correction to the VV-only limit is linear, rather than quadratic, in U/(4​V)U/(4V).

9 All-momentum static observables and Mott–CDW brackets

For each U/t=4,8,…,40U/t=4,8,\ldots,40 in main-text Fig. 5(b), we define VMottV_{\rm Mott} as the largest sampled interaction on the Mott branch and VCDWV_{\rm CDW} as the smallest sampled interaction on the CDW branch. Both endpoints are evaluated on the complete 861-point symmetry-reduced mixed-momentum grid. Branch assignment follows the coincident discontinuities in the ground-state energy slope, double occupancy, checkerboard structure factor, and nearest-neighbor spin correlation. We plot the midpoint

(VU)c=VMott+VCDW2​U\left(\frac{V}{U}\right)_{c}=\frac{V_{\rm Mott}+V_{\rm CDW}}{2U} (S93)

with vertical half-width (VCDW−VMott)/(2​U)(V_{\rm CDW}-V_{\rm Mott})/(2U). Thus the bar reports the directly sampled interval containing the branch crossing, rather than a statistical uncertainty or a fit interval.

The measured static quantities use the following normalizations, with Ns=16N_{s}=16 sites and Nb=2​NsN_{b}=2N_{s} distinct NN bonds:

Di\displaystyle D_{i} ≡1Ns​∑i⟨ni↑​ni↓⟩,\displaystyle\equiv\frac{1}{N_{s}}\sum_{i}\langle n_{i\uparrow}n_{i\downarrow}\rangle, KNs\displaystyle\frac{K}{N_{s}} ≡⟨Hkin⟩Ns,\displaystyle\equiv\frac{\langle H_{\rm kin}\rangle}{N_{s}},
⟨ni​nj⟩NN\displaystyle\langle n_{i}n_{j}\rangle_{\rm NN} ≡1Nb​∑⟨i​j⟩⟨ni​nj⟩,\displaystyle\equiv\frac{1}{N_{b}}\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\langle n_{i}n_{j}\rangle, CNN\displaystyle C_{\rm NN} ≡1Nb​∑⟨i​j⟩⟨𝐒i⋅𝐒j⟩,\displaystyle\equiv\frac{1}{N_{b}}\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\langle\mathbf{S}_{i}\!\cdot\!\mathbf{S}_{j}\rangle, (S94)
Sc​(𝐐)\displaystyle S_{c}(\mathbf{Q}) ≡1Ns​∑i​jei​𝐐⋅(𝐫i−𝐫j)​⟨(ni−1)​(nj−1)⟩,\displaystyle\equiv\frac{1}{N_{s}}\sum_{ij}e^{i\mathbf{Q}\cdot(\mathbf{r}_{i}-\mathbf{r}_{j})}\langle(n_{i}-1)(n_{j}-1)\rangle, Sz​z​(𝐐)\displaystyle S^{zz}(\mathbf{Q}) ≡1Ns​∑i​jei​𝐐⋅(𝐫i−𝐫j)​⟨Siz​Sjz⟩,\displaystyle\equiv\frac{1}{N_{s}}\sum_{ij}e^{i\mathbf{Q}\cdot(\mathbf{r}_{i}-\mathbf{r}_{j})}\langle S_{i}^{z}S_{j}^{z}\rangle,
n⁡(𝐤)\displaystyle n(\mathbf{k}) ≡∑σ⟨c𝐤​σ†​c𝐤​σ⟩.\displaystyle\equiv\sum_{\sigma}\langle c^{\dagger}_{\mathbf{k}\sigma}c_{\mathbf{k}\sigma}\rangle. (S95)

Thus n⁡(𝐤)n(\mathbf{k}) is spin summed and lies between 0 and 2. The charge-density-wave proxy used below is mCDW2=Sc​(π,π)/Nsm_{\rm CDW}^{2}=S_{c}(\pi,\pi)/N_{s}.

The all-momentum calculation supplies the order diagnostics that were absent from the Green-function path data. For each VV, the mixed-momentum grid contains 41 points in each direction. We calculate the wedge 0≤kx≤ky≤400\leq k_{x}\leq k_{y}\leq 40, reflect it under kx↔kyk_{x}\leftrightarrow k_{y}, and use a symmetry weight of two away from the diagonal. Independent half weights at the 00 and π\pi endpoints implement two-dimensional trapezoidal quadrature. A complete set therefore contains 861 solved wedge points and total quadrature weight 1600. All 14 sets at V=0,4,8,9,10,10.01,10.02,10.1,10.2,10.4,11,12,16,V=0,4,8,9,10,10.01,10.02,10.1,10.2,10.4,11,12,16, and 20 are complete.

Figure S8 shows that charge, spin, kinetic, and momentum observables change branch together. The momentum-to-momentum standard deviations of the local observables are O⁡(10−5)O(10^{-5}) near the crossing, so the discontinuity is not produced by a minority of mixed-momentum points. Table S5 lists the two directly adjacent points. The exact energy identity

E0Ns=KNs+U​Di+2​V​⟨ni​nj⟩NN\frac{E_{0}}{N_{s}}=\frac{K}{N_{s}}+UD_{i}+2V\langle n_{i}n_{j}\rangle_{\rm NN} (S96)

holds over all 12,054 calculated points with maximum residual 2.2×10−102.2\times 10^{-10}.

The full n⁡(𝐤)n(\mathbf{k}) maps are shown in Fig. S9. The value V/U=0.25V/U=0.25 is omitted from the phase-labelled rows because it lies at the atomic crossing; its measured values remain in all quantitative analyses. The noninteracting reference has n0​(𝐤)=2n_{0}(\mathbf{k})=2 below the Fermi line, zero above it, and one on the line. Interactions redistribute this step into a smooth band-memory profile whose Brillouin-zone average remains one. Particle–hole symmetry is verified numerically through n⁡(𝐤)+n⁡(π−𝐤)=2n(\mathbf{k})+n(\pi-\mathbf{k})=2 with maximum residual below 7×10−67\times 10^{-6}.

Figure S10 tests the leading strong-coupling description not only for n⁡(𝐤)n(\mathbf{k}) but also for the energy, kinetic energy, double occupancy, and nearest-neighbor density product. To state explicitly which rule is used in each panel, define

ΔM=U−V,ΔC=7​V−U,𝒫NN=14−CNN,\Delta_{\rm M}=U-V,\qquad\Delta_{\rm C}=7V-U,\qquad\mathcal{P}_{\rm NN}=\frac{1}{4}-C_{\rm NN}, (S97)

where 𝒫NN\mathcal{P}_{\rm NN} is the nearest-neighbor singlet-projector weight of the Mott background. With n⁡(𝐤)=1+a​ε𝐤n(\mathbf{k})=1+a\varepsilon_{\mathbf{k}}, the leading predictions are

Mott sideCDW sideE0/Ns2​V−8​𝒫NN/ΔMU/2−4/ΔCa−4𝒫NN/ΔM−2/ΔCK/Ns−16𝒫NN/ΔM−8/ΔCDi8​𝒫NN/ΔM21/2−4/ΔC2⟨ni​nj⟩NN1−4​𝒫NN/ΔM214/ΔC2\begin{array}[]{c|cc}&\text{Mott side}&\text{CDW side}\\ \hline\cr E_{0}/N_{s}&2V-8\mathcal{P}_{\rm NN}/\Delta_{\rm M}&U/2-4/\Delta_{\rm C}\\ a&-4\mathcal{P}_{\rm NN}/\Delta_{\rm M}&-2/\Delta_{\rm C}\\ K/N_{s}&-16\mathcal{P}_{\rm NN}/\Delta_{\rm M}&-8/\Delta_{\rm C}\\ D_{i}&8\mathcal{P}_{\rm NN}/\Delta_{\rm M}^{2}&1/2-4/\Delta_{\rm C}^{2}\\ \langle n_{i}n_{j}\rangle_{\rm NN}&1-4\mathcal{P}_{\rm NN}/\Delta_{\rm M}^{2}&14/\Delta_{\rm C}^{2}\end{array} (S98)

The five rows of Eq. S98 supply, in order, panel (a), panel (b), panel (c), and the two observables in panel (d); panels (b,c) display −a-a and −K/Ns-K/N_{s}. Across the applicable points, the fitted n⁡(𝐤)n(\mathbf{k}) slope differs from the Mott- and CDW-side formulas by at most 1.44% and 0.68%, respectively. This agreement identifies virtual hopping as the origin of the momentum differentiation.

10 Frustrated-hopping robustness

The main text presents a compact t′=−0.25​tt^{\prime}=-0.25t comparison. Figures S11 and S12 provide the complete U/t=8,12,20,U/t=8,12,20, and 40 sequences for t′=−0.25​tt^{\prime}=-0.25t and −0.4​t-0.4t, respectively, while Figs. S13 and S14 give the corresponding VV-only sequences. A continuous low-weight GZ still traverses the gap, but a single rescaling of the complete bare tt–t′t^{\prime} band is not the correct strong-coupling description. Separating

εNN(𝐤)=−2t(coskx+cosky),εNNN(𝐤)=−4t′coskxcosky,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})=-2t(\cos k_{x}+\cos k_{y}),\qquad\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NNN}}(\mathbf{k})=-4t^{\prime}\cos k_{x}\cos k_{y}, (S99)

the minimal fit is

ωGZ​(𝐤)=sNN​εNN​(𝐤)+sNNN​εNNN​(𝐤),sNN<0.\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}(\mathbf{k})=s_{\mathrm{NN}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+s_{\mathrm{NNN}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NNN}}(\mathbf{k}),\qquad s_{\mathrm{NN}}<0. (S100)

The hopping-class moment derivation in Sec. 5 gives, for the two dispersion components retained here,

ωGZ​(𝐤)=4​CNN​εNN​(𝐤)+4​CNNN​εNNN​(𝐤)+O⁡(tmax2/U),\omega_{\mathrm{GZ}}(\mathbf{k})=4C_{\mathrm{NN}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}(\mathbf{k})+4C_{\mathrm{NNN}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NNN}}(\mathbf{k})+O(t_{\max}^{2}/U), (S101)

where CNNC_{\mathrm{NN}} and CNNNC_{\mathrm{NNN}} are nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor spin correlations. The leading spin Hamiltonian has J2/J1=(t′/t)2J_{2}/J_{1}=(t^{\prime}/t)^{2}. The extracted coefficients and the independently calculated 4​CNN4C_{\mathrm{NN}} and 4​CNNN4C_{\mathrm{NNN}} predictions are collected in Table S3. The negative NN coefficient records the inversion caused by CNN<0C_{\mathrm{NN}}<0, whereas the diagonal coefficient remains positive because CNNN>0C_{\mathrm{NNN}}>0; the two spin correlations, rather than one global scale, determine the frustrated GZ dispersion.

Figure S12 shows that the same separation into NN and NNN contributions remains accurate for the stronger frustration t′=−0.4​tt^{\prime}=-0.4t and compares the full GZ dispersion with the corresponding J1J_{1}–J2J_{2} prediction.

The VV-only sequences in Figs. S13 and S14 converge to the distinct CDW-side rule derived in Sec. 6.1: NN hopping carries the local charge-defect coefficient −8/7-8/7, whereas NNN hopping propagates the defect within one checkerboard sublattice and therefore carries unit coefficient. Figures S13(a–d) and S14(a–d) make the separation of scales explicit: the particle-addition and particle-removal bands move apart with VV, whereas the white gap-interior GZ retains an O⁡(t)O(t) dispersion. The curves in panels (e) collapse rapidly with increasing VV, and panels (f) show that at V/t=12V/t=12 the independently fitted NN+NNN form is indistinguishable from −(8/7)​εNN+εNNN-(8/7)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NN}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NNN}}. Increasing |t′||t^{\prime}| from 0.25​t0.25t to 0.4​t0.4t changes the GZ shape through the NNN contribution but leaves the NN and NNN coefficients unchanged, confirming that the CDW-side result is controlled by local defect motion rather than by a new global rescaling.
